name: guard
description: When a turn ends, guard asks the session to run its router subagent over the response; the router names which audit agents would actually find something in it — unsupported claims, deferrals the repo could answer, explanation the reader cannot follow, a Korean answer translated by its own author, unnatural Korean, comments in the source it edited, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that drifted from a map into a payload, saved reference docs that filled up with local reasoning — each with a reason; on a turn they run one at a time, so each one's findings are in the answer file before the next one reads it. A documentation agent reports where the document is — already saved, in the repository, or in a knowledge base the project configures — and fetches and saves the primary source when only the network has it; a saved reference the turn wrote is checked by an auditor of its own. One switch per agent, all off until you turn one on, plus two saved settings for whether a session starts with turn and plan auditing armed — armed unless the project says otherwise, and `guard off` mutes just the session you are in. A separate `interviewer` agent is not part of that: you talk to it directly in its own transcript before any work starts, and it questions you one at a time — testing what you said rather than guessing the rest — until the request is clear, then researches it and, when you close the interview, leaves one brief on disk for the session to act on. A `handover` skill writes a self-contained session handover before you clear the conversation, and the session `/clear` opens next is offered it: guard carries the file's path across that boundary and the session asks whether to read it. Claude Code and Codex. Requires Python 3.11+.

interface.shortDescription: Audit finished turns for unsupported claims
